reason: Screened on 6 Sep 2026 after live re-verification. (1) The row's decision-maker is wrong: it names 'Balázs Balogh, CEO & Co-Founder'; every primary and secondary source found (The Insurer, EU-Startups, Vestbee, The Recursive, Crunchbase, the company's own quotes) names Dušan Komar as Co-Founder & CEO, with Laslo Horvath (CTO) and Dennis Weinbender (Chief Pricing and Data Officer) as co-founders and Luka Bucan as Group COO; no Balázs Balogh is associated with Ominimo. A load-bearing decision-maker claim that does not survive verification blocks a case. (2) The trigger itself is real but smaller than the row implies: on 27-28 Jul 2026 Ominimo announced the first part of an ongoing Series B, EUR 20.1M (USD 22.5M) from EBRD Venture Capital at a EUR 1.4B (USD 1.6B) valuation, 15 months after a EUR 10M Series A from Zurich Insurance Group at EUR 200M; total external funding is therefore about EUR 30M. 'US market entry confirmed for 2027' is in the sources only as a target. (3) Re-scored honestly the signal does not clear the 70 threshold: timing 15, capacity 11 (a profitable Budapest-based managing general agent with ~100 staff, ~EUR 307M annualised gross written premium and ~1M customers in Hungary, Poland, the Netherlands and Sweden, but EUR 30M raised in total; an F1 entry would be a multiple of its equity funding), brand fit 15 (consumer motor insurance is a natural F1 category and the lane is open outside Orion180 at Haas and AON at Ferrari), urgency 12 (European expansion and a 2027 US target), ops fit 9 (MODE B halo only; no team workstream) = 62/100. Keep on the radar: a larger second close of the Series B, or a carrier licence with a marketing budget behind a US launch, would re-open the case; the Hungarian GP (Budapest) and Dutch GP (Zandvoort) sit in its home markets.
